sections.content:
9,080 people

were counted on the census as "pipe fitters" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Pipe fitters install pipe systems and maintain and repair pipes in major utilities, industrial and construction settings and sites.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "pipe fitters" there were more men than women (99% compared with 1%).

This means "pipe fitters" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "skilled metal, electrical and electronic trades".

Men made up 99.1% and women made up 0.9% of "pipe fitters"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "pipe fitters" included:

  • plasterers
  • steel erectors
  • carpenters and joiners

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "pipe fitters" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "pipe fitters", 11.9% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "pipe fitters" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "pipe fitters" included:

  • groundsmen and greenkeepers
  • metal working production and maintenance fitters
  • welding trades

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "pipe fitters", 6.3% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (95.4% compared with 4.6%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (60.7%) than self-employed (39.3%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the North West. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Barrow-in-Furness, this is in the same region of the North West.
